transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (MedBridge CTO), Samir Patel (MedBridge ML Eng), Angela Ortiz (MedBridge DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Onboarding progress: test account created but VPC peering pending; some IAM roles missing.
- Initial benchmarks run: baseline latencies and token costs shared; p50 ~85ms, p95 ~420ms (noisy due to KV cache warmup).
- Action items: Redwood to share security pack; customer to provide VPC details; run second benchmark with representive prompt set.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you carving out time. we' ll do the usual quick status, blockers, then results review. Ethan, you got the numbers?
[00:28] Ethan Ross: yeah, I have the benchmark summary, I'll share screen right after, but quick note: we ran hosted and dedicated comparators — the dedicated pool was configured with 2xA10-ish instances, quantized model q4_0, we saw steady p50 around 85ms for single-turn prompts, p95 around 420ms; there was some tail because of KV cache cold starts and the prompt set had a few long seqs.
[01:12] Laura Chen: okay, so 420ms p95, that's better than we expected, just want to check — is that including our request transformation layer? because we have an ingress lambda that adds about 30 to 40 ms.
[01:26] Samir Patel: yep, our pipeline has an extra ~35ms on average. so end-to-end will be closer to p95 ~455ms, which is kinda at the upper edge of our SLA goal (we target 500ms).
[01:40] Maya Patel: good to know. the Redwood numbers are service-side only, so add your pipeline. Also note we can do prefix caching which should help on repeated user flows.
[01:52] Angela Ortiz: quick onboarding note — I created the test account per the onboarding doc, however VPC peering hasn't been established. our security team needs the peering CIDR and the runbook for peering. I put a request in the ticket but no response.
[02:10] Maya Patel: ah okay, that's on us — I'll escalate the peering doc and the exact CIDR range. Ethan, can you paste the VPC peering details in the ticket after the call?
[02:22] Ethan Ross: yep will do. I'll also include the KMS key guidance — you mentioned wanting customer-managed keys for the Private deployment.
[02:31] Laura Chen: yes, for any PHI we need customer-managed keys and audit logs. SOC 2 attestation is necessary too. do you have a SOC 2 report?
[02:40] Maya Patel: yes, we'll share the SOC 2 type II summary and the security pack. we'll redact sensitive bits but it has the controls mapping you need. sending by Mon the 10th.
[02:50] Samir Patel: thanks. On the benchmark, were you using the same model weights as our plan? we planned to run a 13B open model with 8-bit quantization, not q4_0 — those differ a bit.
[03:05] Ethan Ross: good point. the initial run used a 13B variant that we have tuned (q4_0), but I can re-run with the exact pinned weights and the 8-bit pipeline you mentioned. response quality was comparable in quick evals but we'll do a controlled comparison.
[03:20] Maya Patel: pragmatically, the POC is to validate latency and unit cost at your traffic profile. Samir, can you remind us of the expected concurrency and token averages?
[03:30] Samir Patel: expected steady 25 concurrent users with spikes to 50 for short windows, average prompt length ~120 tokens, completion ~80 tokens. so roughly 200 tokens per request.
[03:45] Ethan Ross: okay that helps — we can simulate 50 concurrent with batching thresholds and show cost tradeoffs. batching will reduce cost but increase tail latency; we can tune batch timeout to meet your 500ms SLA.
[03:58] Laura Chen: can you explain the batching tradeoff again? we saw some docs but it's fuzzy to non-infra folks.
[04:06] Maya Patel: sure — batching groups incoming tokens across users to run through the kernels together which amortizes GPU work and lowers tokens-per-dollar. but waiting for a batch means small extra latency. Redwood provides policies: latency-first (small batch size), cost-first (larger batches), and adaptive which tries to hit a latency SLO while still batching when possible.
[04:28] Angela Ortiz: are those controls available in Private deployment or only hosted?
[04:33] Ethan Ross: both. the runtime exposes the same batching config regardless of deployment — Dedicated or Private — we surface it in the console or via the config API. Private will also give you control over autoscaling and compute limits.
[04:47] Laura Chen: PII concern — how do you handle logging and KV cache? we can't keep user prompts in logs.
[04:55] Maya Patel: by default we mask/store minimal metadata. for Private, you can disable persistent logs or integrate with your logging endpoint. KV cache is ephemeral and can be configured to not persist to disk; we also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[05:10] Samir Patel: great. on the last run we saw some inference errors where tokens clipped — suspecting tokenization mismatch with our preprocessor. how should we validate?
[05:20] Ethan Ross: send a canonical set of inputs and we'll run a tokenization parity check. sometimes tokenizers differ across toolkits; we'll record the token counts and the model's input ids to compare.
[05:30] Maya Patel: ok Samir, action item — share the prompt set by Monday.
[05:35] Samir Patel: yes will do.
[06:00] [--- Quick pause while Maya and Ethan talk off-mic briefly about scheduling ---]
[06:30] Ethan Ross: back on benchmarks — I want to call out the cold start behavior: first few requests had higher p95 (~900ms) due to KV cache warm and some compilation jitter. after warmup within 20-30 minutes we saw stable numbers. for POC we recommend an explicit warmup run before the measured window.
[07:00] Laura Chen: that makes sense. for our production we will have periodic keep-alive pings.
[07:10] Angela Ortiz: about the peering — we need a test account with restricted access (no write to production) and a runbook to reproduce the peering. can Redwood set up a restricted test account?
[07:23] Maya Patel: yes, we can create a restricted test role and a temporary API key bound to the test CIDR. we'll include the steps in the runbook.
[07:35] Samir Patel: another question on cost: can you show unit cost per 1k tokens for the configuration? we need to map to our budget.
[07:45] Ethan Ross: initial estimate: for the dedicated config we used, unit cost came to approximately $0.18 per 1k tokens at our utilization — with batching that can go down to ~$0.09 per 1k tokens. hosted has slightly higher list price but no infra management. those numbers are approximate — we'll provide a detailed cost spreadsheet.
[08:05] Laura Chen: can you annotate which costs assume quantization and which assume full fp16?
[08:12] Ethan Ross: yes — q4_0 and 8-bit quantization materially reduce memory and allow denser packing; I'll split the sheet by quant level.
[08:20] Maya Patel: also note, Dedicated reserved capacity pricing differs if you commit monthly vs on-demand; we'll include the reserved vs on-demand comparison in the doc.
[08:33] Angela Ortiz: about security/compliance again — beyond SOC2, we need SSO (SAML) + RBAC so we can tie roles to our internal groups. is SAML supported?
[08:45] Maya Patel: yes we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user sync; RBAC is configurable in the console, and you can map to your groups. I'll attach the SSO guide.
[08:56] Samir Patel: for Private deployment, any special network reqs beyond peering? firewall rules?
[09:02] Ethan Ross: typically just peering and routes; for on-prem there are a few firewall ports (gRPC ports) to open. we'll provide a checklist.
[09:12] Laura Chen: okay — if we get peering done by next Tues, can you run the 2nd benchmark Wed/Thu?
[09:20] Ethan Ross: yes that's doable. we just need the test account creds and the prompt set.
[09:25] Maya Patel: let's confirm dates: action items — Angela to send peering info by 2026-05-12, Samir to send prompts by 2026-05-11, Ethan will run benchmarks 2026-05-13 and share artifacts.
[09:40] Angela Ortiz: that timeline works. one more minor thing — we tried the console earlier and saw a permissions error when attempting to view logs. maybe the test account didn't have the right role.
[09:51] Maya Patel: thanks for flagging — we probably scoped down the role too far. I'll correct and push a new role that allows log viewing in the sandbox only.
[10:05] [Interruption, background noise — someone on customer side taking a call briefly]
[10:40] Ethan Ross: switching topics quickly — quantization deep-dive: we saw a small delta in output quality between q4_0 and 8-bit on one of your safety prompts, likely due to activation clipping. we can run a fine-tuning pass or use dynamic per-layer dequant to mitigate.
[11:05] Samir Patel: what's the expected engineering effort for that?
[11:10] Ethan Ross: for the mitigation it's mostly model-side config and a couple of hours to test; for fine-tune it's more involved and probably out of scope for the POC. we'll try config first.
[11:22] Laura Chen: also want to loop in our security reviewer next week for a short meeting — can Redwood join with someone from security?
[11:30] Maya Patel: yes, we can have our security solutions engineer join; how about Tue 2026-05-12 16:00 UTC?
[11:40] Laura Chen: that works, I'll invite our security reviewer.
[12:00] Maya Patel: quick recap before we end: 1) Redwood to share SOC2 + security pack by 2026-05-10; 2) Angela sends VPC peering details and test account needs by 2026-05-12; 3) Samir sends canonical prompt set by 2026-05-11; 4) Ethan runs benchmark and shares raw logs on 2026-05-13; 5) schedule quantization deep dive for week of 2026-05-18.
[12:25] Samir Patel: sounds good, thanks all.
[12:30] Laura Chen: thanks, appreciate it.
[12:35] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread with the docs and links.
[12:40] [Meeting ends]
